name: JavaScript Handbook
articles: Variables
Use "const" for a value that stays the same and "let" for one that will change. Do not use "var" in new code.
variable variables const let var declare value store

Functions
A function is a named piece of code that takes values in and gives one back. The short arrow form does the same.
function functions arrow return parameters arguments define call

If and else
An "if" runs code only when its condition is true. Use === to compare, which also checks the type.
if else condition conditional compare equals check true false

Loops
A "for" loop counts; "for … of" goes through the items of a list; "while" repeats as long as something is true.
loop loops for while repeat iterate count each of
js
Arrays
An array is an ordered list. "push" adds to the end, "map" makes a new list from it, and "filter" keeps only some items.
array arrays list push pop map filter find length items

const nums = [3, 8, 12];
nums.push(20);                               // [3, 8, 12, 20]
const doubled = nums.map(n => n * 2);        // [6, 16, 24, 40]
const big = nums.filter(n => n > 10);        // [12, 20]
const first = nums.find(n => n > 5);         // 8
console.log(nums.length);                    // 4

Work with text
Strings have methods to change case, cut pieces out, search and split. Backticks let you put values inside text.
string strings text upper lower split join replace includes template length

const name = 'Ada Lovelace';
console.log(name.toUpperCase());          // ADA LOVELACE
console.log(name.includes('Love'));       // true
console.log(name.split(' '));             // ['Ada', 'Lovelace']
console.log(`Hello, ${name}!`);          // Hello, Ada Lovelace!
